story.title: Hunter Biden Reports Worsening Condition of Joe Biden's Cancer
story.summary: Hunter Biden has revealed that his father's prostate cancer has worsened, stating it has metastasized into his bones and is causing significant pain. He described the situation as 'very debilitating' and expressed the emotional toll it takes on the family during a recent interview.

explore_lenses.label: What is actually new in this update?
explore_lenses.title: A reported progression, not the first bone finding
explore_lenses.summary: Joe Biden’s cancer was publicly described as metastatic to bone when it was diagnosed in May 2025. Hunter Biden’s new account indicates that it has spread “further” and is now causing substantial pain, but it does not specify new sites, scan results, or a change in formal staging.

claims.text: Biden’s office said in May 2025 that he had Gleason 9 (Grade Group 5) prostate cancer with bone metastasis and that it appeared hormone-sensitive.
Hunter Biden said in an August 8, 2026 interview that the cancer had metastasized into his father’s bones “and further,” and called the pain and debility severe.
The available reporting does not identify additional organs involved, the extent of progression on imaging, PSA results, or whether the disease has become resistant to hormone treatment.

explore_lenses.label: Why does painful bone spread matter?
explore_lenses.title: Bone metastases can drive pain and complications
explore_lenses.summary: Bone involvement is a central source of illness in metastatic prostate cancer: it can cause pain and can raise risks including fractures and spinal-cord compression. Symptoms can be treated, but their severity does not by itself reveal prognosis or the effectiveness of Biden’s current therapy.

claims.text: The American Cancer Society says prostate cancer that has spread commonly reaches bone and that bone metastases can cause pain, fractures, spinal-cord compression, and dangerous high calcium levels.

The National Cancer Institute lists pain medication, external-beam radiation, radiopharmaceuticals, denosumab, bisphosphonates, and corticosteroids among treatments for bone pain associated with metastatic prostate cancer.
Hunter Biden characterized his father’s pain and impairment as “very painful” and “very debilitating,” describing the family’s observed experience rather than a medical assessment.

explore_lenses.label: What is known about treatment and next steps?
explore_lenses.title: Care will depend on treatment response and symptoms
explore_lenses.summary: Biden completed a course of radiation therapy in October 2025, while his longer-term treatment plan was not publicly specified. For metastatic prostate cancer, clinicians commonly tailor systemic treatment and symptom-directed care to disease response, prior therapies, comorbidities, and the location and extent of metastases.

claims.text: A Biden spokeswoman told CBS in October 2025 that he had completed several weeks of radiation therapy; the report said it was then unclear whether additional treatment would be needed.

NCI says metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer is commonly treated with androgen-deprivation therapy combined with another hormone therapy, and some patients receive chemotherapy as part of intensified treatment.

Forecast: NCI guidance indicates that future management would ordinarily be determined by whether the disease remains hormone-sensitive or has progressed despite treatment, as well as symptoms and metastatic extent; this is a general clinical framework, not a prediction of Biden’s care.

story_report.summary: Hunter Biden said his father, former President Joe Biden, has prostate cancer that has spread further after metastasizing to his bones. In an Aug. 8 interview, Hunter Biden described the illness as “very painful” and “very debilitating,” saying the progression has imposed a severe physical burden on his father and an emotional strain on the family. No clinician or Biden representative has publicly provided new details about the extent of the reported progression.

sections.heading: Joe Biden’s Earlier Cancer Disclosure
sections.body: Biden’s office said in May 2025 that he had Gleason 9, Grade Group 5 prostate cancer with bone metastasis, and that the disease appeared hormone-sensitive. A Biden spokeswoman later told CBS that he had completed several weeks of radiation therapy in October 2025, though it was unclear at the time whether further treatment would be needed. Hunter Biden’s recent account indicates progression beyond what had previously been publicly described.

sections.heading: Bone Metastases and Cancer Pain
sections.body: Prostate cancer commonly spreads to bone, according to the American Cancer Society, and bone metastases can cause pain as well as fractures, spinal-cord compression and dangerously high calcium levels. The National Cancer Institute lists pain medicines, external-beam radiation, radiopharmaceuticals, denosumab, bisphosphonates and corticosteroids among treatment options for bone pain associated with metastatic prostate cancer. Hunter Biden’s description reflects the family’s observation of his father’s condition, not a medical assessment.

There is no public statement from Biden’s physicians on his current medication, treatment response, next appointment or prognosis; reports also do not specify which bones are affected, whether skeletal complications have occurred, or how pain is being managed.

related_stories.title: Japan Commemorates 81st Anniversary of Nagasaki Atomic Bombing
related_stories.summary: On the 81st anniversary of the atomic bombing of Nagasaki, Mayor Shiro Suzuki condemned the increasing global support for nuclear deterrence, asserting that 'humanity and nuclear weapons cannot coexist.' He labeled nuclear weapons as 'absolute evil' and urged the Japanese government to uphold its non-nuclear principles established after World War II.

related_stories.summary: Typhoon Dolphin has made landfall on China's eastern coast, bringing sustained winds of up to 162 km/h. The storm is expected to continue affecting the region into Monday, with reports of over 1,600 flight cancellations and evacuations as residents prepare for the impact.

related_stories.title: Court Halts Trump's White House Ballroom Construction Pending Congressional Approval
related_stories.summary: A federal appeals court has ruled that construction of President Trump's $400 million ballroom at the White House must be halted until Congress grants explicit approval. The court agreed with a lower court's decision that such a significant renovation requires congressional consent.
